newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Four Nigerian oil communities threaten Shell.
newsitem.headline: Four Nigerian oil communities threaten Shell.

text.p: Four communities in Nigeria's ethnically-fragmented south have given Royal Dutch Shell a July 8 deadline to leave their oil-producing area or be forced out, local newspapers reported on Thursday.

The newspapers said a letter from the ethnic-Ijaw communities near Sokebelou in Delta State accused Shell of not providing local people with benefits from the 75,000 bpd of crude oil pumped into flow-stations in the area.
"Shell must go if she does not change her shameless stand of disregard for the goose that lays the golden egg in this nation," the independent Thisday newspaper quoted the letter as saying.

The communities involved recently won a battle against Shell in local courts over compensation of around 30 million naira ($350,000) for environmental damage, but now say Shell is planning to appeal to a higher court.
"Naturally we take this seriously and we are always ready to talk to local communities," a Shell spokesman in Lagos said.
"In this case the communities should understand that we are acting within our rights to appeal against a court decision that we should pay compensation."

The spokesman said no compensation could be paid for the 1982 oil spill, from the trans-Forcados pipeline, because it was found to have been caused by sabotage. He said Shell cleared up the spilled oil.

Ethnic clashes in March between Ijaw and Itsekiri tribesmen at nearby Warri forced Shell to close several oil wells earlier this year after fighting erupted over the relocation of a local government headquarters.

Shell came under fire from campaigners in 1995 after the execution for murder of author Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other activists who campaigned for rights for the southeastern minority Ogoni community and against alleged pollution by Shell.
Shell pumps around half of Nigeria's roughly two million bpd crude oil production.
